lines: These files are public by design, so what gitleaks matches in them is not reported:
appinfo/signature.json, the integrity signature: 26 matches in what ships, 37 matches in 3 commits.

In these generated files gitleaks matches only rules that take any string of high entropy, which hashes and minified names are as well, or the curl lines a page of built documentation copies from its source, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
vendor/symfony/validator/Constraints/PasswordStrength.php, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
A key a build takes from the environment ends up in such a file too: where one of them has no reason to carry a key, look at it.

These files are test data, the report of a test run or example code, whose keys and tokens are made up or serve a test, so the matches are not reported as secrets. Those of a private key or a GitHub token are:
tests/Unit/EntitlementServiceTest.php, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
A token a test run used against a real server stays valid until it is revoked: where one of these files holds one, revoke it.
